title: Stanford Law School CodeX: legal informatics center landing page
answer: This is the Stanford Law School CodeX landing page, a partnership between the Law School and the Department of Computer Science. It says CodeX explores how information technology can enhance legal processes, and that data science and artificial intelligence help gain a quantitative and predictive understanding of the law. The most useful point is that its research aims to move beyond traditional empirical analysis and build sophisticated computational models of legal systems. The page also lists programs on agentic AI applications, a legal technology hackathon, an international conference, and FutureLaw 2026.

sections.body: Stanford Law School publishes this CodeX landing page. CodeX is described as a partnership between the Law School and the Department of Computer Science. The page introduces the center and lists several programs and events. It does not state a publication date. It mentions FutureLaw 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: CodeX is presented as a partnership between Stanford Law School and the Department of Computer Science. Its stated purpose is to explore how information technology can enhance legal processes. The page says data science and artificial intelligence help gain a quantitative and predictive understanding of the law. It adds that CodeX research aims to move beyond traditional empirical analysis to build sophisticated computational models of legal systems. The page then lists activities. One is a hands-on accelerated program for interdisciplinary Stanford student teams designing and prototyping agentic AI applications at the intersection of technology and law. Another is a hackathon uniting AI innovators, machine learning specialists, and legal professionals to prototype the future of legal technology. A third is an international conference uniting leading legal experts, policymakers, and business leaders to harness AI for sustainable, ethical, and responsible legal systems. The page also mentions FutureLaw 2026, which brings together global leaders in law, technology, and policy to explore how computational law and legal AI can answer these challenges. The text is brief and functions mainly as an introduction to the center and its events rather than a detailed research report.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no statistics or numeric findings. It names FutureLaw 2026 as an event. It defines CodeX as a partnership between Stanford Law School and the Department of Computer Science. It states that data science and artificial intelligence help gain a quantitative and predictive understanding of the law, and that CodeX research aims to move beyond traditional empirical analysis to build sophisticated computational models of legal systems. It also describes an accelerated program for Stanford student teams, a hackathon, and an international conference.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in the legal industry can use this page as a short orientation to Stanford CodeX and its stated interests. It connects legal AI to computational law, agentic AI applications, legal technology prototyping, and responsible legal systems. It also points to named activities such as a hackathon, an international conference, and FutureLaw 2026, which may be useful for finding events or research communities. Because the page is an introduction, it is most useful as a signpost to CodeX rather than as evidence about how legal AI performs in practice.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: The page is a brief landing page. It does not provide research findings, methods, case studies, statistics, or outcomes. It does not state a publication date. It is an institutional overview rather than a commercial vendor page. It is partial because it only summarises CodeX and its activities, and it does not compare legal AI tools or discuss adoption in law firms or courts.
